findings.likely_cause: The hero's position on the planet ('al') is animated procedurally on top of in-place skeletal clips. (1) The walk-in uses E.out, so the root starts at about 3x its average speed (~3 u/s) while 'Walk' strides at a constant ~1 u/s. (2) The +0.14 rad lunge and -0.06 rad recoil are applied to position, not rotation. (3) The teeter adds +0.05*wob*sin(2.6 Hz) rad (+/-0.15 u) to position. Also 'Walk' starts exactly at the cut with a 0.05 s crossfade from the default Idle.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the feet planted and move all body motion into rotation about the feet. (1) Walk-in: al = lerp(0.02, 0.32, prog(tt, G1 - 0.3, G1 + 0.6, E.lin)), with hero.play(G1 - 0.3, 'Walk', {fade: 0, speed: rootSpeed/strideSpeed}) so the cut lands mid-stride and the stride matches the root. (2) After the walk, hold al constant: delete the '+ 0.14*prog(...)', '- 0.06*prog(...)' and '+ 0.05*wob*Math.sin(...)' terms from line 319-320. Express them as a lean instead: lean = 0.10*prog(tt, G1+0.5, G1+1.2, E.inOut) - 0.05*prog(tt, G1+1.3, G1+1.6, E.out); hero.root.quaternion.setFromEuler(new THREE.Euler(al + lean + pitch, 0, 0, 'XYZ')). The existing pitch term already gives a pivot-on-the-feet teeter.

findings.what_viewer_sees: The ~250 white 'nine in ten of us' city dots blink off within 2-3 frames, while the equator ring, split bar, overlay and pill around them all fade out smoothly over 0.4-0.6 s. At speed it reads as an off-switch, not a fade, and is out of keeping with their staggered 0.7 s grow-in.
findings.evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-juicytea-media/4a181100-5b6b-5601-bf64-5ea13c092764/scratchpad/review6/grab_s1/xt_00752_16x1_c960-900-400-60.jpg: all dots at full brightness through f761 (25.37 s). About 90% are gone at f762, only a few faint ones remain at f763, none at f764. Over the same frames the equator ring fades gradually from f752 to f764.
findings.likely_cause: The fade-out factor is multiplied into 'ca' and then pushed through the staggered gain k = clamp((ca*1.25 - 0.25*i/N)*4). k stays saturated at 1 until ca < 0.4, then drops to 0 by ca 0.2 for the eastern cities and by ca 0 for the western ones. ca follows a cubic inOut, so the planned 0.6 s fade (25.02-25.62) collapses to about 25.34-25.45 for almost all dots.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the stagger for the grow-in only and apply the exit as a plain alpha multiplier: const cin = prog(tt, t.nine - 0.1, t.nine + 0.6, E.lin), cout = 1 - prog(tt, t.s006 + 0.3, t.s006 + 0.9, E.inOutSine); skip if cin*cout <= 0; k = clamp((cin*1.25 - i/N*0.25)*4); radius from k; ctx.globalAlpha = 0.25*k*cout for the halo and 0.95*k*cout for the core.

findings.likely_cause: Double easing. The k passed to printKB is prog(tt, t.breath - 0.4, t.africa13 - 0.2), which already applies prog's default E.inOut. The call also passes ease: E.inOut, which printKB applies again (ch1_fx.js:51), giving inOut(inOut(x)): peak slope 3x3 = 9x average, with long flat ends.

result.intended_notes:
Detector events judged intended and reading well:
- E1, E2: South America and Africa highlights pop from 0.3 to 1.0 alpha, with a pop SFX, 0.08 s before each word.
- E3-E5, E7, E8, E10-E12, E14-E16, E19, E20, E25-E27: designed hard cuts, each within 0.1 s of its narration word. E7 and E8 bracket the 1-second paleo flash (white flash fades over 4 frames). E16 is the deliberate 1.4 s cut to black on 'Eventually'.
- E6: coin outBack pop-in.
- E13: tetrahedron snaps back to a sphere with outBack overshoot plus the red X on 'wrong'. The overshoot frames shade cleanly; the 2D yellow wire keeps its full tetra size for ~3 frames as it fades, which is acceptable.
- E17, E18: fade-up from black and the 0.5 s dissolve to the 1620 title page.
- E21: second Bacon page slams in with outExpo.
Defects: E9 is S1-3, E22 is S1-7, E23/E24 are S1-8.

Other deliberate snaps that read fine:
- Cold-open inOutExpo whip from Africa to India (about 6 fast frames, f170-f176).
- Coin freezes face-on in one frame on "They're not" (f877->f878), cracking two frames later.
- Fog-globe expo dive to the pole (f2382-f2389), timed to "continent... down there?".

Stretches checked at full frame rate and clean:
- 0-7.7 s cold open (arcs, pops)
- 7.7-16.2 s flat map, pills and drip arrows
- 18.8-30.06 s north/south globe (overlay, equator ring, bar, pill swap, coin) apart from S1-2
- 31.1-38.3 s headline globe
- 45.1-51.8 s tetrahedron and the fast spin
- tiles and the black hold
- 54.5-61.8 s map fade-up, sepia wipe and 2026->1620 counter
- portrait and page Ken Burns
- 69.35-75.35 s Africa/South America globe and 'accident' page
- 75.35-85.8 s fog dive, 1620->1820 ticker and Antarctica reveal
Narration sync is within 0.1-0.2 s everywhere except S1-4.

Chunk seams checked with frame-exact grabs: f449/450, f899/900, f1349/1350, f1799/1800, f2249/2250. No look change at any of them; the coin alpha across f899/900 matches the code (the coin is drawn as stacked layers that share one alpha, so it reads more opaque than nominal). No other runtime material toggles of the ch2_sets kind in ch1.

Side notes:
- shots.js camAt reads only the destination key's ease, so 'ease' on keys[0] is silently ignored at ch1.js:411, :426, :443 and :537. For example, the 'last' spin was meant to accelerate (E.in) into the 'crash' tiles but decelerates instead. Smooth, but not what was written.
- tools/grab.py can mislabel frames by +1. Its '%.4f' seek plus default CFR image2 muxing duplicates the first frame when the rounded seek lands more than half a frame early (e.g. 'grab.py 876 28' labels the f902 flash as f903). Adding '-fps_mode passthrough' fixes it. A frame-exact replacement is at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-juicytea-media/4a181100-5b6b-5601-bf64-5ea13c092764/scratchpad/review6/s1work/exact.py; all frame numbers above come from it.
- Composition only: at 'those southern points' (26.1 s) Cape Froward is behind the limb and Kanyakumari is at the limb edge.
- The README audio flags (voice tail cut at 28.56; impact_deep masking 'Eventually' at 53.10-53.75) were not assessed.
